where_in_legend: myelin_inv06_20261107/output/README.md and evidence (GSK3 sign in oligodendroglia divided); gsk3_inv09 R05, R06
note: Report states Wnt negatively regulates OL maturation as settled; module holds opposing arms (GSK3 inhibitors raised differentiation while Wnt3a inhibited it in optic-nerve culture; SB216763 opposed differentiation after Foxg1 knock-down). Audit (vf-09, full text of 42274605): the review also supports the report's Wnt-negative premise (sec. 3: continuous Wnt signalling reduces differentiation of oligodendrocyte progenitors), so the premise itself is not contradicted; what is divided is the GSK3-inhibition sign (the same review: lithium promotes differentiation; abstract: inhibition associated with differentiation).

PMID 38123002 is solifenacin (a selective M3 antagonist) in cuprizone mice; Wnt inhibition is a downstream observation of that drug, and the paper does not manipulate GSK-3. The report's wording presents it as Wnt inhibition as such.

PMID 42274605 is a 2026 review; its abstract says inhibition of GSK-3 beta is associated with oligodendrocyte differentiation: the opposite direction to the use the report makes of it (supports harm). Abstract only. Split from E11 after the audit. The review holds both directions side by side (abstract and sec. 3 lithium sentence favourable to GSK-3 inhibition; sec. 3 Wnt-negative sentence unfavourable to Wnt activation; sec. 4 inhibition increases neuronal differentiation in neural progenitors, opposite to F005; secs. 6-7 no direct remyelination evidence in patients). No review sentence supports "GSK-3 beta inhibition impairs oligodendrocyte differentiation"; classed superseded_or_contradicted for the report's use, not for the Wnt premise.
